title: ZnO Nanoparticles-Modified Unsaturated Polyester Resin Composites: Structural, Mechanical Properties and Surface Stability Under Sewage Sludge Exposure
content: Unsaturated polyester resin (UPR) composites containing 0.02–1.00 %wt. ZnO nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) were prepared using an MEKP–cobalt octanoate curing system and evaluated for sanitary sewer components. The influence of ZnO NPs content on chemical structure, hardness, tensile and flexural properties, scratch resistance, thermal behaviour, and surface characteristics was investigated using FTIR, XRD, mechanical testing, TGA, DSC, optical surface analysis, and SEM. Based on the initial screening, composites containing 0.06, 0.75, and 1.00 %wt. of ZnO NPs were selected for detailed characterisation and subsequent 28-day exposure to activated sludge. The effect of ZnO NPs content was not uniform across the investigated properties. Among the comprehensively characterised formulations, 0.06 wt.% ZnO NPs provided the most favourable overall balance, retaining a tensile strength of 41.20 ± 2.08 MPa while increasing Td,5% from 359.6 °C for pristine UPR to 368.4 °C and Tmax from 410.9 to 422.5 °C. No statistically significant mass changes were observed after activated-sludge exposure, indicating good bulk stability. However, surface roughness and heterogeneity increased, with Ra rising from 0.26 to 1.01 µm for the 0.06%_ZnO NPs composite. Overall, this formulation appears the most promising for further development toward sanitary sewer applications.
